newsitem.title: USA: Florida doctor who gave lethal injection charged.
newsitem.headline: Florida doctor who gave lethal injection charged.

text.p: A doctor who admitted giving a dying patient a dose of deadly potassium chloride to end his suffering has been indicted on a first-degree murder charge, his attorney said Tuesday.
Dr. Ernesto Pinzon, 36, will appear before a judge Wednesday and ask to be released on bond, attorney Roger Craig said.
Pinzon was indicted by a grand jury Thursday and arrested as he waited for a plane to carry him to Puerto Rico, where he has relatives. He entered a plea of not guilty, Craig said.
Pinzon has retained Geoffrey Fieger, who has successfully defended assisted-suicide crusader Dr. Jack Kevorkian in three trials, as his criminal lawyer.

Pinzon gave patient Rosario Gurrieri, a 70-year-old man dying of lung cancer, an injection of potassium chloride, Valium and morphine Oct. 6. Potassium chloride is often used in lethal-injection executions to stop the heart.
Gurrieri died an hour later. The grand jury held that neither the patient nor his family asked that Pinzon administer a lethal dose.
Craig said Pinzon used a relatively small dose that would not necessarily have killed the patient and could have boosted the effectiveness of the morphine.
